statement: A top-5 developer reports AI systems did >= 50% of code or experiments in a frontier training project (technical report or system card; by 2028-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met in 2023. No developer reported an AI share of code or experiments in a frontier training project. Related signals: a coding assistant vendor claimed its tool wrote 46% of code among its users (general software, not frontier training), and a top-5 developer set a 4-year goal of building an automated alignment researcher.

items.summary: A major code-hosting platform claimed its AI pair-programmer was 'already writing 46% of code' for its users and helped developers code up to 55% faster; a general-software usage claim, not a frontier-training-project measurement.
items.detail: GitHub blog, Thomas Dohmke, 'GitHub Copilot X: The AI-powered developer experience', 2023-03-22 (page notes an update on 2024-05-21; the 46% figure appears in the original announcement text).

items.summary: A top-5 developer launched a team with 20% of its secured compute, aiming within four years to build a roughly human-level automated alignment researcher - an explicit plan to automate parts of AI research.
items.detail: OpenAI, 'Introducing Superalignment', 2023-07-05 (co-led by Ilya Sutskever and Jan Leike).

items.summary: No 2023 technical report or system card from a top-5 developer quantified the share of code or experiments done by AI in a frontier training project; the metric did not yet exist publicly.
items.detail: Checked in-phase frontier disclosures opened this run: GPT-4 System Card (2023-03), Gemini launch post (2023-12-06), Preparedness Framework beta (2023-12-18) - none report such a share.
